Count maps out of a coproduct by adding the counts for the two channels instead of multiplying.
Claim Real_0 has an element when neither channel is posited; the construction alone yields none.
Claim positing a structure channel posits a difference channel; the two posits are independent.
Claim that not every pair of maps out of the channels extends to the coproduct; the universal property gives exactly one extension for every pair.
Swap which channel a retraction lands in: with an empty difference channel the retraction onto structure exists, not onto difference.
Take the coproduct of two one-element channels to have one element (a join) instead of two.

claim_boundary.supports: Kernel-checked for arbitrary types PD, S, with Real0 PD S given the two-constructor shape of OntologyBasic.Real0: both injections are injective, their ranges are disjoint and exhaustive, Real0 is equivalent to PD + S, every pair of maps out of the channels has exactly one extension (universal property), and the number of maps out of the coproduct is the product of the numbers of maps out of the channels (|C|^(|PD|+|S|)). A map out of the coproduct that is the identity on one channel (a retraction onto it) exists iff that channel is nonempty or the other channel is empty: a retraction onto the difference channel is impossible only when that channel is empty and the structure channel is not (and symmetrically); whenever both channels are inhabited retractions in both directions exist (retractions_both_ways_of_nonempty), each one of |A|^|B| choices that the coproduct does not select. So bare function-existence is trivial for inhabited channels and does NOT formalise "no reduction of either channel to the other". Real0 is nonempty iff a channel is, empty for two empty channels, and all four combinations of the two nonemptiness posits are realised, so neither posit follows from the construction or from the other. Native exhaustive tables: 38 map counts (|A|,|B| <= 2 with |C| <= 3, plus (3,2,2) and (2,3,2)), 16 retraction tables for |A|,|B| <= 3, and the four-row posit table; the injection, disjointness and covering columns are set facts built from the tags, so the kernel theorems are the evidence for them.
